Mochi has some GEN... and a question: how can it help keep GenLayer honest?
On GenLayer, validators are the ones who check the work.
When an Intelligent Contract needs a decision, several validators look at it independently, then vote on whether the answer holds up.
To earn a seat, a validator stakes GEN. That's its skin in the game.
Do the job well, and it earns rewards. Act dishonestly, and part of that stake can be slashed.
Mochi doesn't want to run a validator. So Mochi can delegate:
back a validator it trusts with its GEN, and share in that validator's rewards... and its risks.
Pile everything onto one giant validator, and the whole network leans on a few shoulders.
Spread it across several reliable ones, and more independent voices help decide.
If it were me? I'd spread it out.
Stake carefully. Delegate wisely. Keep GenLayer decentralized.
